title: Two fds, one file
question: dup(fd) gives a second fd for the same open file. What do the two share?
text: An fd is only a number; behind it is the open file, a `struct file`. Two fds can stand for the same one: `dup`.

1. [fget_raw](2:fget_raw) finds the open file fd 3 stands for, and counts one more reference to it; [get_unused_fd_flags](2:get_unused_fd_flags) takes the lowest free slot, 4; [fd_install](2:fd_install) puts the same `struct file` there. [What it changed](2:fd_install:memory): `fd_array[4]`, the same file as `fd_array[3]`.
2. The position is the open file's, not the fd's: the read through fd moves `f_pos` from 0 to 5 ("hello"), and [the read through fd2](4:ksys_read) goes on from 5 (" from"): see `buf`.
Try: [open it twice instead](try:1): two opens make two open files, each with its own position, so the second read starts at 0 again.
